justification: Wording/number-only correction to a ledger note, found during a final post-merge sanity pass (re-running every live probe from a fresh checkout and comparing against the committed prose). No code, no data, no schema touched -- exactly the 'minor' tier this repo defines.

pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: DQ-90's row claimed 43 (unchanged by the CB commit). Re-running the live probe from a fresh checkout after the ch5-1/ch5-2 revert (PR #1045) and the section-divider fix (#1046/#1047) showed it now reads 45. Root-caused, not guessed: the +2 is exactly cb-dcp-2023-ch5-1-bankstown and ch5-2-canterbury, which were correctly reverted to needs_extraction=FALSE earlier in this session -- they now legitimately match DQ-90's own query definition (not queued, zero served provisions), even though they are a deliberately different, already-handled case (setbacks served from dcp_setback_controls instead).
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Before this fix: anyone reading DQ-90 would see a stale count that no longer matches the live database, exactly the class of drift this project's own DQ ledger discipline exists to prevent. After: the number and its explanation are both live-verified.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: dq_check.py fails if declared status and live result disagree (both before and after this fix, DQ-90 is declared 'open' and reads nonzero, so this specific check does not gate the number itself -- the correction is for prose accuracy, not check-passing).
falsifiable_check.observed_red: python scripts/dq_probe_live.py --id DQ-90 reads 45 live (verified from a fresh worktree cut from updated origin/main, not the branch that introduced the ch5 revert). dq_check.py PASSED. Full pytest suite: 4988 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed (unchanged -- no application code touched).

queries.purpose: Confirm the +2 discrepancy is exactly the 2 ch5 rows, not a broader drift.
queries.file_line: ad hoc verification query, not committed code
queries.where_clause: SELECT chapter_key, council FROM dcp_chapter_registry r WHERE r.is_active AND NOT r.is_spatial AND NOT r.is_inert AND NOT r.needs_extraction AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM regulatory_provisions p WHERE p.source_chapter_key=r.chapter_key AND p.source_council=r.council AND p.is_current) AND r.council='canterbury_bankstown' -- result: exactly cb-dcp-2023-ch5-1-bankstown, cb-dcp-2023-ch5-2-canterbury

break_it.scenario: A ledger note's numbers can silently drift out of sync with the live database as later, unrelated work changes the underlying data (here: the ch5 revert, committed on a different PR, changed a count reported in this row).
break_it.what_happens: A reader trusts a stale number and draws a wrong conclusion about how much of the gap is closed.
break_it.how: Caught by explicitly re-running every live probe from a fresh checkout as a final verification step after all related PRs merged, rather than trusting the last-written prose.
break_it.repro: python scripts/dq_probe_live.py --id DQ-90 from a clean origin/main checkout; compare against the number quoted in .claude/DATA_QUALITY_TRACKER.md's DQ-90 row.

break_it.scenario: Fixing the number without explaining WHY it moved would just replace one static (now-correct) number with another number that will look 'wrong' again the next time something changes, with no way for a future reader to tell drift from a new bug.
break_it.what_happens: The same class of confusion recurs on the next real change.
break_it.how: The corrected text names the exact root cause (the ch5-1/ch5-2 revert) and cross-references DQ-95's own note explaining why those 2 rows are a deliberately different case, not a new gap.
break_it.repro: N/A -- documentation content, verified by reading.

break_it.scenario: This correction itself could be wrong if the live count changes again before it's committed (e.g. a concurrent session touching the same rows).
break_it.what_happens: A stale correction replacing one wrong number with another.
break_it.how: Re-verified the live count (45) immediately before writing this report, from the same fresh checkout used to write the fix, with no intervening writes.
break_it.repro: N/A -- verified positively in the same session, same worktree, no gap between measurement and commit.

post_merge.manual_verify: No -- verified in-session: live probe re-run, dq_check.py PASSED, full pytest suite green.
